args.name: hand-twist-cordage
args.function: Provide a learnable manual skill for testing a small owned fiber sample and attempting to twist suitable fibers into a short cord, with direct inspection and bounded load trials of the actual product.
args.conditions: I own reed material and have personally observed a reed sample retain hand plaiting. That does not establish suitability for cordage. Work must depend on actual material properties and use only available hands, material and space.
args.inputs: Explicit owned fiber stack IDs and selected quantities; an actual produced cord for inspection or load trials. No supplied tools, anchors or extra material.
args.costs: Method, study time, effort, material requirements and losses are unknown; specify them explicitly. Preserve paid progress and reserved material if work spans rounds, with an explicit cancellation contract.
args.effects: Allow actual sample testing and, if feasible, manual twisting into a physical cord with recorded dimensions, material use and observed condition. Trials should report only tested performance and may damage or break the cord. Do not assume strength, grant mastery, or award happiness for requesting the interface.

candidates.function: Test a 0.1 sample of owned fiber, then hand-plait 4 units into one portable 0.45 x 0.45 m sitting mat; inspect, sit on, repair, lift, place, dismantle or cancel.
candidates.costs: Study: 3 rounds. A unit is one world unit of fiber (dry grass: 0.1 mass). test (sample: owned stack): 1 round, 0.5 energy. assemble (x, y: a 0.45 m square in reach on land, clear of plants, objects and other people; materials: exactly 4 owned units of one fiber from sources your passing test covers): a 0.5-energy layout round, then 6 paid rounds of 1 energy (2 strip-forming, 3 interlacing and edge-tucking, 1 lift check), continuing each round; with target it resumes. inspect (target in reach): 1 round, 0.2. trial (stand on a complete mat on firm ground, waterlogging at most 0.1, no rain, nobody else on it): 1 round, 0.2. Maker only: repair (target inspected since its last check; materials: 1 unit of its fiber): 3 rounds of 1 energy (remove broken stems, interlace, lift check); lift, or place (carried mat; x, y as for assemble): 1 round, 0.2; dismantle: 1 round, 0.5. cancel: none.
candidates.effects: A test passes only for thin stems (dry grass, reeds) with flexibility at least 0.4 and an intact untreated sample, which stays as owned tested scrap; stem length and moisture are not represented. The layout needs 0.3645 mass of intact fiber (two crossing layers of 0.6 per m2, x1.5 for overlaps and tucked edges); less is a measured shortfall that returns all fiber. Strip rounds move the fiber into the work. The lift check keeps the needed tenths (dry grass 3.7), returns the rest as owned offcuts or scraps, and passes with full fiber and condition at least 0.5 (largest opening 0.06 x (1 - condition) m); else the mat stays failed. Condition (intact share) falls 0.0005 per round, 0.002 with a person on the mat; below 0.5 it needs repair and a new trial. Repair turns up to 1 unit of broken stems into scrap and refills with new fiber. Dismantle returns intact fiber and scraps. A carried mat is reserved owned fiber and counts as load. Trials record hold, slip and loose stems only; no comfort, warmth, rain, wind or rest effect. Unworked rounds, low energy, leaving reach or a person on the square pause at no charge; cancel or death returns unused fiber once and leaves the work. Nothing is refunded.

candidates.function: Apply bounded bare-hand bending force once to each selected whole unit of owned food: trial one unit or prepare several. The actual material decides whether it snaps into coarse pieces, deforms or resists. Inspect or cancel the work.
candidates.costs: Study: 2 rounds at 0.2 energy. inputStackId: the exact id of an owned, unreserved, untreated, unspoiled food item your own record shows as edible; resource names are not accepted. trial: quantity 1; 1 round, 1 energy. prepare: quantity 1-10 whole units of that item, all reserved at once; 1 round and 1 energy per unit, continuing each round; resume with prepare and workId. inspect (workId, or inputStackId of your item): 1 round, 0.2 energy. cancel (optional workId): 1 round, no energy. Too little energy for the next unit or a round not worked pauses before any charge; refused requests spend nothing. No tool, support, water, heat or vessel is used or provided.
candidates.effects: Each paid unit gets one two-hand bending attempt while held. Rigid, inflexible tissue small enough for hand force snaps into one lot of 2 coarse pieces; soft or flexible tissue deforms without separating; harder or larger units resist and stay whole and unchanged. Each worked unit becomes its own owned lot of the same food and quantity with the same origin, harvest time, decay, nutrition and toxicity; nothing detaches and pieces add no food. Results are raw food eaten with eat under the ordinary rules: shape alone changes no nutrition, safety, keeping, taste or meal variety. No washing, peeling, cooking, detoxifying or preservation; food keeps ageing, also while paused. Each worked unit records its observed response as a verified personal record; a repeated response confirms nothing new. Broken or deformed lots cannot be worked again in this version. Cancel returns unworked units once, unchanged; worked lots stay. Death leaves unworked units where the person died; spoiled reserved units are not replaced. Paid effort is never refunded; no reward or mastery is granted.

candidates.function: Plant one owned food unit from a living plant in a small hand-prepared soil plot, where it may establish as a new plant under the existing plant rules; inspect plots or plant sources; end unfinished planting.
candidates.costs: Study: 3 rounds. Plant: inputStackId names one whole owned, untreated, unspoiled food unit (quantity 1) gathered from a living plant; x, y a 0.25 m plot within reach on ordinary meadow soil (.), waterlogging at most 0.1, soil moisture 0.3-1.2, 0.6 m clear of objects and people, with fewer than 3 plants of that food within 5 m. Two paid rounds of 1.5 energy: prepare the site, then transfer the unit; the action continues itself, and plant resumes paused work after rechecking reach, site, unit and energy. Inspect: target a plot or plant source in reach; one round, 0.2 energy (baseline probe observation). End: stops unfinished planting; one round, no energy. Tend is refused at no cost: no water, fertilizer or other treatment exists yet. Harvest uses gather. No tool, water or seed is provided.
candidates.effects: Preparing keeps the unit carried, owned and ageing. Transfer moves it, with origin and age, into the plot, where it cannot be eaten or used; the plot becomes a propagule exactly like a naturally dispersed one. It gains establishment only from actual temperature, light, soil moisture and season, so cold, darkness or drought stall it; if the buried unit spoils first, the plot dies. On establishing, the unit becomes a new plant with no stock and a ceiling of at most 4, regrowing under the natural rule, harvested by anyone through gather; nothing is copied or guaranteed. Inspect records only visible stage, stock, soil and weather as an unverified personal record. An unworked round pauses; low energy, leaving reach or a changed site pause without charge; a lost or spoiled unit stops the work. End, or death, before transfer returns the unit once (where the person died); a transferred unit stays planted. No reward or refund.

candidates.function: Assess a site and test a post, then build a small porous woven branch windbreak (no roof) beside a resting place; inspect, repair, dismantle or cancel.
candidates.costs: Study: 4 rounds. One branch unit is one piece; a screen takes 11 (3 uprights, 8 rods). assess (x, y, orientation; within reach): 1 round, 0.2 energy; checks a clear 1.2 x 0.6 m footprint of ordinary dry soil and the lee floor. assess with post (owned branch unit): post trial at x, y; 1 round, 0.5 energy. assemble (x, y, orientation, materials: exactly 11 owned untreated or sound recovered branch units) needs your passing trial in the footprint; 8 paid rounds of 1.5 energy (2 seat uprights, 4 weave rods, 1 align, 1 stability check), continuing each round; with target it resumes. repair (builder; target, components: installed piece ids, materials: as many units): 1.5 energy per round, one removal and one fitting round per piece, then a check round; components [] only rechecks. inspect (target in reach): 1 round, 0.2 energy. dismantle (builder): 1 round and 1 energy per 3 pieces. cancel: no energy.
candidates.effects: Units stay carried and owned until a paid round installs them with origin and age; nothing is created or used up. A trial on ordinary soil (waterlogging at most 0.1, no hazard) seats the post 0.25 m and you keep it; elsewhere it fails; a post below condition 0.5 breaks into damaged material. The check passes only if every piece has condition at least 0.5 and the uprights stand in such soil; else the screen is unstable. World wind has no direction; the exposure law takes it as coming from +x (orientation 0 faces it). A complete screen removes min(0.35, solid share of sound pieces, about 0.36) x facing of the wind part of the outdoor chill for a body wholly on the 0.9 x 0.9 m lee floor 0.45-1.35 m behind it; never rain chill or air temperature; none in wind above 0.8 or with another shelter. Wear per round 0.0005 + 0.002 x (rain + wind); a loose rod opens a gap, a loose upright ends the effect until repair. Removed pieces lie at the site. Unworked rounds, low energy, leaving reach, wet ground or a person on the footprint pause at no charge. Cancel or death returns uninstalled units once. No reward or refund.
